final_text:
CAUSE: The worktree name for each call drops the occurrence counter that makes identical calls distinct, so byte-identical calls get the same worktree name. Your teammate's stale-directory guess isn't the cause.

Evidence:
- `ValueError: worktree already exists` is raised in `create_worktree` (`app/workspace.py:581-582`). It fires when `WORKTREE_ROOT/<repo_slug>/<name>` already exists.
- `wf_run.py` `_call_key` (around line 517) returns `f"{sha256(payload)}:{occurrence}"`. The occurrence counter is what separates identical calls. Ten identical calls give `<digest>:0` through `<digest>:9`, all with the same digest.
- In the call path (around line 818), the worktree name is `name = f"wf-{self.run_id[:24]}-{call_key[:12]}-a{attempt}"`. `call_key[:12]` is only the first 12 hex characters of the digest. The `:N` suffix is cut off.
- So all 10 identical calls get the same name, for example `wf-<run>-<digest12>-a0`.
- With concurrency 3, the first call creates the directory. The next call's `wt_path.exists()` check then fails, and the error aborts the stage.
- Calls with different prompts have different digests, so they never collide. That matches what you see.
- The other per-call paths already use the full key. The scratch dir at line 655, the step file at line 775 and the archive at line 857 all use `call_key.replace(":", "-")`. Only the worktree name loses the suffix.
- A fresh run directory and an empty `git worktree list` are consistent with this. The collision happens inside the run, between sibling calls. `create_worktree` holds `repo_mutation_lock`, but the lock only serialises the calls. The second one still sees the first one's directory.
- I did not run a reproduction. This comes from reading the code.

Recommended fix:
- In `wf_run.py`, build the name from the full key with the colon replaced, for example `call_key.replace(":", "-")`. Alternatively, use `digest[:12]` plus `-o{occurrence}`. The result is `wf-<run24>-<digest12>-o<N>-a<attempt>`.
- The name must stay deterministic. Resume and retry rely on the same call getting the same name, so don't use a random suffix.
- Check the branch name too. It is `feat/<slug>/<name>`, so it becomes unique once the name does. Without this fix, a duplicate branch would hit "checked out in another worktree" as well.
- Add a regression test that runs several identical calls with `tools="all"` and asserts the worktree names are all different.
